original_question: Does there exist an absolute constant B such that for every positive integer N one can choose an integer a relatively prime to N for which the sum of all continued-fraction coefficients of a/N is less than B log N?
target_in_paper: Section 2, Conjecture 2 (Moser), stated immediately after Conjecture 1 (Zaremba) in the discussion following Theorem 2.7 on two-dimensional lattice point sets. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1407.2380))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's intended target almost verbatim: it asks for an absolute constant, quantifies over every positive integer N, requires choosing a coprime integer a, and uses the weaker sum-of-continued-fraction-coefficients bound B log N rather than the stronger bounded-partial-quotient version of Zaremba's conjecture. That is exactly the paper's Conjecture 2. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1407.2380))
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone, it should specify that the continued-fraction coefficients are the partial quotients in the finite simple continued fraction expansion of a/N, e.g. a/N = [0; a1, ..., ar]. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1407.2380))

It should normalize the choice of numerator as 1 <= a < N, so that a/N is explicitly a reduced rational in (0,1); this is implicit from the surrounding lattice-point-set context immediately preceding the conjectures. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1407.2380))
It should state explicitly that the constant B is absolute, i.e. independent of both N and the chosen numerator a. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1407.2380))

If maximum paper-faithfulness is desired, it should identify the statement as Moser's conjecture and note that the paper presents it as a weaker version of the preceding Zaremba conjecture. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1407.2380))
refined_question: Is Moser's conjecture true: does there exist an absolute constant B > 0 such that for every integer N >= 1 there exists an integer a with 1 <= a < N and gcd(a,N) = 1 for which, writing a/N in finite simple continued-fraction form as a/N = [0; a1, ..., ar], one has sum_{j=1}^r a_j < B log N?
justification: The draft is clearly targeting Conjecture 2 in Section 2, not a broader neighboring problem, because the paper states this conjecture with the same quantifier structure and the same B log N bound on the sum of the continued-fraction coefficients of a/N. The nearby context first states Zaremba's stronger bounded-coefficient conjecture as Conjecture 1, then gives the present statement as the weaker conjecture attributed to Moser, and finally records only a one-way consequence for discrepancy bounds of 2-dimensional lattice point sets. Since the paper does not state an equivalence here, no alternate equivalent formulation should be supplied. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1407.2380))
